repeat device-add or formatting. Never modify the seed after leaves depend on it.

Neither stage performs seed transport, Incus creation, identity registration or
startup. They have no identity/backend preflight dependency.
Those later steps remain subject to the owner's manual
script comparison. The existing identity mode described below expects an
unpartitioned leaf and must not be used with this new partitioned image.

The upgrade lifecycle is host → container only, using Btrfs without Unison:

```sh
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
```

partition 2 during provisioning, including when the first upgrade is empty.
Subsequent synchronization sends incrementally from the retained
common baseline, including deletions within the upgrade tree. Received baselines stay read-only;
the published upgrade `@` is a writable clone. Transfer intents and prior
versions are retained for recovery; interrupted publication is not retried
automatically. Snapshot retention cleanup is not implemented by this stage.

The chatbot runit startup invokes `boot` for explicitly paired storage before
starting the container. It restores existing loop/mount attachments, synchronizes,
then publishes a read-only OverlayFS OS view at `.mounts/NAME/root-view`.

uses the installed seed. Patches removing seed files must include OverlayFS

or read-only policies remain in effect, with private persistence bound separately.

views before rotating a lower layer; it never changes Btrfs membership.

its identity-root integration remains part of the subsequent provisioning step.

The seed has the seven sibling subvolumes and guest systemd FUSE service.

per-instance documents: their content is changed in each private writable leaf,
not in the sealed seed. Shared owner links expose cognitive memory, skills,
routing and plugins without granting authority or starting those features.

The following describes the earlier helper contract. Its device paths,
host-owned FUSE attachment and early backend gates are not the new manual
partitioned-disk workflow and still require reconciliation before automation.

currently named `/dev/sdb2`. Each container has its own writable leaf. A leaf

after release activation, the operator entrypoint is

and provisioning preflight operations through their `call` files. It checks
the operation receipts before invoking the read-only
`op-identity-root seed-preflight`, followed by `seed-profile`, before creating
an empty Incus instance with the `3tched-lungs` profile.
The helper checks the physical seed identity, SEEDING flag and block read-only
state, and refuses a direct mount of the physical source. The wrapper holds
a per-session lock; the helper serializes seed loop setup and leaf creation.
`seed-create` adds the new private writable leaf once. Later starts mount
that existing leaf; stopping does not remove a Btrfs member. Failed starts
also retain membership. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage;
its `attached` field describes logical attachment, not device membership.
The session hostname and private persistence are
created through the sprout, so those writes belong to the leaf. Persistence is
an ordinary mode-0700 directory at `@agent_user/persist`, bound to the guest's
`/opt/run-mounts/persist`. Provisioning creates no subvolumes at all: only the
seven inherited members are used. Agent soul,
and shared subvolumes remain protected in the guest view. Rules and user
preferences are instance-specific and writable in each private leaf.

Storage receipts identify this layout as `shared-partition-siblings-v2` and
pin its inherited subvolume identities plus the persistence directory's inode,
parent subvolume identity, sprout FSID and image metadata digest. The directory must remain on its
parent filesystem and cannot be a symlink, separate mount, or subvolume.
Older v1 receipts with an extra `@persist` subvolume and snapshot-based receipts are
rejected; this change does not silently migrate them or replace existing
container roots. Existing live persistence and older containers are neither
deleted nor converted; replacement must be prepared separately. Historical
soul reconciliation now verifies existing subvolumes and native devices only,
and fails when they are missing instead of creating them.

Before sealing a new base, `op-identity-image prepare TOP RELEASE_ID
PROVENANCE_JSON` records the archive provenance, offline package inventory,
critical file hashes and exact seven-member layout. It also prepares ordinary
mountpoint directories under `@/run/mount/3tchedFS` and `@/run/opdbus/lungs`.
The helper does not download or verify the archive signature, mount storage,
toggle SEEDING, format devices or create subvolumes. See
[image preparation](../../../deploy/workspace-image/README.md) for its input
contract. Creation fully verifies the pristine image before adding a leaf;
later checks verify the pinned metadata without rejecting legitimate private
package updates in the leaf.

FUSE runs on the host. Fresh provisioning selects a persistent Incus `disk`
device named `3tched`, exposing the session's own host FUSE mount at
`/run/mount/3tchedFS`. The seed needs an empty destination directory, not a
guest FUSE daemon. A native instance UUID pins the host source and process
receipt. An existing legacy hook receipt is verified without silently
converting its attachment mechanism. The common `/etc/3tched` directories
are a separate read-only Incus disk attachment, with links from the inherited
agent subvolumes.

The `3tched-lungs` Incus profile supplies these inherited devices:

```yaml
config: {}
devices:
  runtime-run:
…
    readonly: "true"
```
…
See the [Btrfs seeding documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pin the manually prepared GPT/overlay instance for identity-owner adoption.
# No format, member changes, start, credentials, grants or identity-store writes.
set -euo pipefail
fail() { printf 'prepare-chatbot-adoption: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
[[ $# == 1 && $1 =~ ^(3tchedCtlChatbot|3tchedChatbot|ID-[1-9][0-9]*)$ && ${#1} -le 63 && $(id -u) == 0 ]] || fail 'usage (host root): prepare-chatbot-adoption NAME (existing configured chatbot)'
umask 077
name=$1

sid=b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28
key=[REDACTED:opaque-base64]
operator=${OP_3TCHEDFS_EXPECTED_SESSION-414fbc56-03fb-20ab-758a-bcc7a7cbdc0e}
client=${THREETCHED_FS:-/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/bin/3tched-fs}
control_mount=${OP_3TCHEDFS_MOUNT:-/run/mounts/3tchedFS}
# --expected-session checks the existing mounted caller; it does not inject an
# identity or use a different principal when admission fails.
[[ -x $client && $operator =~ ^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$ ]] || fail 'mounted client or canonical expected caller session absent'
command -v timeout >/dev/null || fail 'timeout is required for bounded preflight'
pool=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
disk=$pool/.provisioning/$name.json
container=$pool/.provisioning/$name.incus.json
plans=/var/lib/op-dbus/identity-provision-plans
[[ -f $disk && ! -L $disk && -f $container && ! -L $container ]] || fail 'operator preparation receipts absent'
exec 9>"$pool/.provisioning/$name.lock"
flock -n 9 || fail 'instance preparation active'
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg image "$pool/$name.img" '
    .name==$name and .image==$image and .filesystem_prepared==true and
    .phase=="filesystems-prepared" and .layout=="raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1"
' "$disk" >/dev/null || fail 'disk preparation incomplete'
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" --arg key "$key" \
    --arg root "/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$name/rootfs" \
    --arg view "$pool/.mounts/$name/root-view" '
    .version==1 and .name==$name and .session_id==$sid and .phase=="root-bound" and
    .root_bound==true and .upgrade_paired==true and .root_view_readonly==true and .identity_registered==false and
    .threetched_root==$root and .root_view==$view and .instance.name==$name and .instance.type=="container" and
    .instance.config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and .instance.config["user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key"]==$key and
    (.instance.config["volatile.uuid"]|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$"))
' "$container" >/dev/null || fail 'configured chatbot root binding differs or is already adopted'
native_uuid=$(jq -er '.instance.config["volatile.uuid"]' "$container")
if [[ ! -e $plans && ! -L $plans ]]; then mkdir -m 0700 "$plans"; fi
[[ $(realpath -e "$plans") == "$plans" && $(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$plans") == 0:0:700 ]] || fail 'unsafe private plan directory'
[[ ! -e $plans/$sid.json && ! -L $plans/$sid.json ]] || fail 'existing plan must be reconciled; never overwrite it'
work=$(mktemp -d "$pool/.provisioning/$name.adoption.XXXXXX")
printf 'Private preparation evidence: %s\n' "$work"
args=$(jq -cn --arg key "$key" '{wireguard_pubkey:$key}')
if ! timeout --kill-after=5s 30s "$client" invoke --mount "$control_mount" --expected-session "$operator" --args "$args" \
    plugins/identity_sled/operations/inspect_provision_preflight/call > "$work/preflight-receipt.json" \
    2> "$work/preflight-diagnostic"; then
    cat "$work/preflight-diagnostic" >&2
    fail 'owner preflight failed; retain evidence and do not retry through another identity or transport'
fi
# Keep only revision/native metadata; no SID1 is read or copied.
# V4 accepts only a fresh key or the exact explicit-deletion tombstone, as
# validated by identity_clean_provision.rs. Existing bound identities stay out.
jq -ce --arg sid "$sid" --arg key "$key" '
    select(.plugin_id=="identity_sled" and .method=="inspect_provision_preflight") |
    .result | select(.success==true and .plugin_id=="identity_sled" and .method=="inspect_provision_preflight") |
    .result | select(.session_id==$sid and .wireguard_pubkey==$key) |
    select(.previous_instance==null and .previous_native_instance==null and .previous_instance_etag=="") |
    select((.expected_revision==0 and .expected_revision_operation_id=="") or
        ((.expected_revision|type)=="number" and .expected_revision>1 and
         .expected_revision<=9007199254740991 and .expected_revision==(.expected_revision|floor) and
         .expected_revision_operation_id==("delete-provision-"+$sid+"-"+((.expected_revision-1)|tostring)))) |

+The current GPT workflow uses a sparse QEMU raw image under
+`/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/3tched-pool`. This must be the top-level Btrfs
+mount (`FSROOT /`, root ID 5, inode 256) with filesystem UUID
+`a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd`, backed by the Incus pool image
+`/var/lib/incus/disks/3tched.img`. The logical Incus pool is still `3tched`.
+The host root filesystem is not an acceptable fallback; symlink aliases,
+unmounted directories and another filesystem are rejected. A root:root0755
+pool root is supported, but `.provisioning` remains root:root0700 and its
+receipts and instance images remain root:root0600. V4 adoption also verifies
+that the instance image is on the pinned pool filesystem.
+
+The shared seed is the separate protected LVM volume
+`/dev/mapper/3tched--vg-3tched--seed`, UUID
+`8468cc14-a5e4-409c-96f6-1e157d470ab5`. It must remain SEEDING and block
+read-only; no instance identity or Cozo binding is written into it. Adoption
+resolves the unique physical partition or LVM volume rather than a UUID alias
+that may point at its loop, and verifies the read-only loop's complete backing
+against that physical source. Linux 6.17 and newer cannot mount the standalone
+seed and a sprouted filesystem simultaneously; the host mount owner must
+reconcile the standalone seed mount and its boot declaration before pairing.
+This is not permission to modify the seed or replace its read-only loop proof.

PUT 52.=53:
+Pairing sends a read-only snapshot of host upgrade `@` on
+`/dev/mapper/3tched--vg-3tched--upgrade`, UUID

+including when the first upgrade is empty. The host's current top-level mount
+is `/run/mount/3tched-ct-upgrade`; `@` is read-only and its parent stays writable
+for synchronization snapshots. The helper uses the existing host-upgrade mount
+alias under the canonical pool's `.mounts` directory.
PUT 60.=61:
+The base-owned `identity-roots` service selects completed GPT boot receipts,
+verifies the existing native UUID/session/key, and invokes `boot` before a
+separate container start. It restores existing loop/mount attachments, synchronizes,
PUT 73.=74:
+Root binding accepts the exact prepared UID and GID mapping (host 1000000,
+namespace 0, range 1000000000) from `volatile.idmap.next` when a stopped,
+never-started candidate has no `volatile.idmap.current`. If both exist, they
+must agree; no guest start is used to manufacture the current map.
+
+The `--prepare-adoption` stage writes the existing V4 plan for the mounted
+identity owner's digest-pinned adoption operation; it does not adopt, start,

+stages the selected helper closure but does not install or enable the
+base-owned `identity-roots` service or bootstrap its pool mount. Source
+changes alone do not establish installed boot wiring or a completed adoption.
*** End Patch

# Shared physical seed and private leaves

## Manual provisioning checkpoint: partitioned instance disk

The October 11 manual workflow uses a sparse QEMU raw image under
`/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool`, mounted from `@3tched-leaf-pool` on the host's
main Btrfs pool. This subvolume isolates the storage path, but shares that
pool's capacity. The shared seed remains the separate sealed 20 GiB partition;
no instance identity or Cozo binding is written into it.

The completed image preparation step is available through the provisioner:

```sh
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-disk 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --inspect-disk 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-filesystems 3tchedChatbot \
  --seed-device /dev/disk/by-uuid/3415d575-7224-4484-9e0d-06854ac5f032
```

Preparation creates a 60 GiB sparse raw image with GPT: 20 GiB root and the
remaining approximately 40 GiB upgrade partition. `--root-gib` and
`--upgrade-gib` select capacities on a new image. The upgrade remainder is
slightly smaller than its requested capacity because GPT and alignment consume
space. The image and a private preparation receipt live in the leaf pool;
the receipt pins the image inode and both partition identities. An interrupted
creation retains its intent and image instead of retrying or cleaning them up.
`inspect` does not register or adopt an existing image.

The filesystem stage attaches a read-only loop view of the sealed seed and adds
the blank root partition once as its writable leaf. It inherits the seven seed
subvolumes; it does not copy the root or create replacement agent subvolumes.
Only the upgrade partition is formatted, with one `@` subvolume. Shared and soul
are read-only in the leaf; memory, rules, skills and user are writable. Private
persistence directories are ordinary directories. Both mounts stay attached for
the next manual step. The receipt records loops, mounts and fresh filesystem
UUIDs. Interrupted intents require investigation, and prepared receipts cannot
repeat device-add or formatting. Never modify the seed after leaves depend on it.

Neither stage performs seed transport, Incus creation, identity registration or
startup. They have no identity/backend preflight dependency.
Those later steps remain subject to the owner's manual
script comparison. The existing identity mode described below expects an
unpartitioned leaf and must not be used with this new partitioned image.

The upgrade lifecycle is host → container only, using Btrfs without Unison:

```sh
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
```

Pairing sends a read-only snapshot of host upgrade `/dev/sdc3` (`@`) to
partition 2 during provisioning, including when the first upgrade is empty.
Subsequent synchronization sends incrementally from the retained
common baseline, including deletions within the upgrade tree. Received baselines stay read-only;
the published upgrade `@` is a writable clone. Transfer intents and prior
versions are retained for recovery; interrupted publication is not retried
automatically. Snapshot retention cleanup is not implemented by this stage.

The chatbot runit startup invokes `boot` for explicitly paired storage before
starting the container. It restores existing loop/mount attachments, synchronizes,
then publishes a read-only OverlayFS OS view at `.mounts/NAME/root-view`.
The upgrade layer takes precedence over the seed-root layer; an empty upgrade
uses the installed seed. Patches removing seed files must include OverlayFS
whiteouts: deleting a file from the upgrade tree alone reveals its seed copy.
The Btrfs layers receive the container UID mapping before mounting OverlayFS,
because this kernel rejects mapping the merged overlay. The view is bound at
the Incus-managed `identity-roots` rootfs, preserving its pool definition.
Six agent subvolumes are separately bound into `/agent`; their existing writable
or read-only policies remain in effect, with private persistence bound separately.
User contents are never sent or received. Synchronization detaches stopped OS
views before rotating a lower layer; it never changes Btrfs membership.
This new image is not yet admitted by the older unpartitioned root-owner lifecycle;
its identity-root integration remains part of the subsequent provisioning step.

The seed has the seven sibling subvolumes and guest systemd FUSE service.
`@agent_rules/rules/rules.md` and `@agent_user/user/user.md` are initial
per-instance documents: their content is changed in each private writable leaf,
not in the sealed seed. Shared owner links expose cognitive memory, skills,
routing and plugins without granting authority or starting those features.

## Earlier unpartitioned-leaf integration

The following describes the earlier helper contract. Its device paths,
host-owned FUSE attachment and early backend gates are not the new manual
partitioned-disk workflow and still require reconciliation before automation.

Identity provisioning uses one immutable Btrfs seed on the physical partition
currently named `/dev/sdb2`. Each container has its own writable leaf. A leaf
stores that container's changes; it does not contain a copied root filesystem.
Golden preparation includes the wrapper and its helpers under `libexec/3tched`;
after release activation, the operator entrypoint is
`/usr/local/libexec/3tched/provision-workspace-subscriber`.

The seed's top-level layout is `@`, `@agent_memory`, `@agent_rules`,
`@agent_shared`, `@agent_skills`, `@agent_soul`, and `@agent_user`. Provisioning
uses these existing subvolumes in the sprout. It does not create snapshots,
send/receive root filesystems, copy seed images, or use an overlay root.
Readonly loop views reference the same physical partition bytes.

`provision-workspace-subscriber.sh` first verifies the mounted operator
3tchedFS session and sealed catalog, then calls the declared identity inventory
and provisioning preflight operations through their `call` files. It checks
the operation receipts before invoking the read-only
`op-identity-root seed-preflight`, followed by `seed-profile`, before creating
an empty Incus instance with the `3tched-lungs` profile.
The helper checks the physical seed identity, SEEDING flag and block read-only
state, and refuses a direct mount of the physical source. The wrapper holds
a per-session lock; the helper serializes seed loop setup and leaf creation.
`seed-create` adds the new private writable leaf once. Later starts mount
that existing leaf; stopping does not remove a Btrfs member. Failed starts
also retain membership. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage;
its `attached` field describes logical attachment, not device membership.
The session hostname and private persistence are
created through the sprout, so those writes belong to the leaf. Persistence is
an ordinary mode-0700 directory at `@agent_user/persist`, bound to the guest's
`/opt/run-mounts/persist`. Provisioning creates no subvolumes at all: only the
seven inherited members are used. Agent soul,
and shared subvolumes remain protected in the guest view. Rules and user
preferences are instance-specific and writable in each private leaf.

Storage receipts identify this layout as `shared-partition-siblings-v2` and
pin its inherited subvolume identities plus the persistence directory's inode,
parent subvolume identity, sprout FSID and image metadata digest. The directory must remain on its
parent filesystem and cannot be a symlink, separate mount, or subvolume.
Older v1 receipts with an extra `@persist` subvolume and snapshot-based receipts are
rejected; this change does not silently migrate them or replace existing
container roots. Existing live persistence and older containers are neither
deleted nor converted; replacement must be prepared separately. Historical
soul reconciliation now verifies existing subvolumes and native devices only,
and fails when they are missing instead of creating them.

Before sealing a new base, `op-identity-image prepare TOP RELEASE_ID
PROVENANCE_JSON` records the archive provenance, offline package inventory,
critical file hashes and exact seven-member layout. It also prepares ordinary
mountpoint directories under `@/run/mount/3tchedFS` and `@/run/opdbus/lungs`.
The helper does not download or verify the archive signature, mount storage,
toggle SEEDING, format devices or create subvolumes. See
[image preparation](../../../deploy/workspace-image/README.md) for its input
contract. Creation fully verifies the pristine image before adding a leaf;
later checks verify the pinned metadata without rejecting legitimate private
package updates in the leaf.

FUSE runs on the host. Fresh provisioning selects a persistent Incus `disk`
device named `3tched`, exposing the session's own host FUSE mount at
`/run/mount/3tchedFS`. The seed needs an empty destination directory, not a
guest FUSE daemon. A native instance UUID pins the host source and process
receipt. An existing legacy hook receipt is verified without silently
converting its attachment mechanism. The common `/etc/3tched` directories
are a separate read-only Incus disk attachment, with links from the inherited
agent subvolumes.

The `3tched-lungs` Incus profile supplies these inherited devices:

```yaml
config: {}
devices:
  runtime-run:
    type: disk
    source: "tmpfs:"
    path: /run
    initial.mode: "0755"
  lungs-socket-dir:
    type: disk
    source: /run/opdbus/lungs
    path: /run/opdbus/lungs
    readonly: "true"
```

The bridge service creates its existing shared socket at
`/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock`. Mounting its dedicated parent directory keeps
socket replacement visible to each guest without exposing other host runtime
files. `seed-profile` creates this exact profile if absent and rejects existing
configuration drift. Provisioning also verifies the inherited devices and
rejects local overrides. The `/run` tmpfs is mounted before its child devices;
image directories alone would not establish that boot ordering.

The bridge creates a root-owned socket with mode 0666 beneath the root-owned
0755 directory. Connection permission allows negotiation; each operation still
requires an authenticated identity and its existing capability grant. Host
`Bind(session)` requires UID 0 in the bridge's own user and PID namespaces.
Guest `BindCurrentContainer()` takes no session argument: it pins the socket's
original process with SO_PEERPIDFD and derives identity from the exact running
native container. Process, native UUID and authoritative identity are checked
again for each call. No SID1 file is installed in the guest.

Clean replacement is scoped to the configured chatbot key and service identity
`b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, using the provisioner's configured native
alias `3tchedCtlbot`. Hostname remains the session UUID. The old native instance
must be stopped or authoritatively absent, and the new name and leaf must be
unused. Explicit retirement uses `identity_sled.delete_provision_record` through
the operator's mounted namespace, with the existing human write capability
and exact revision. This removes the current row and retains an audit tombstone;
startup respects that tombstone. A version3 plan permits fresh provisioning
from that exact deletion receipt. Ordinary missing rows are not accepted.
After host storage/mount
preparation, the wrapper submits a digest-pinned private plan through the
supported `identity_sled.provision_container` operation. The owner atomically
creates fresh current-schema state and binds it to the new native instance;
legacy persistence and record fields are not imported. Existing external
capability policy remains in force. Normal provisioning starts through
`touch_session`; `--no-start` leaves the fresh identity parked. Only verified
completion receives a boot-ready marker.

If creation fails, `op-identity-root seed-inspect NAME` reports sanitized
receipt metadata and recovery guidance without mounting, formatting or
retrying device-add. Preserve the receipt, base, leaf and mappings until the
recorded intent and actual membership have been reconciled.

Preparing or changing the live seed is a separate operator action. The helper
does not set or clear SEEDING, format the partition, or unmount an unrelated
source mount. Once leaves depend on a seed, that seed must remain unchanged.
At boot, the host storage service uses `seed-readonly` to verify the physical
partition identity and existing SEEDING state, then restore its volatile block
read-only flag before restoring opted-in roots. This never changes filesystem
membership or the SEEDING flag.
The current source change has not been deployed or validated with concurrent
live containers on the fresh base. The September 30 file-backed and physical
seed experiments did demonstrate independent writes, peer-active remounts and
cold loop recreation using distinct read-only views of the same seed on this
kernel. That evidence does not validate this new image/layout or a full host
reboot. There is no fallback to copied seeds if a kernel rejects the shared
arrangement. The owner's current sequencing instruction defers all tests until
after deployment; a successful build alone is not a workflow validation.

See the [Btrfs seeding documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

from that exact deletion receipt. Ordinary missing rows are not accepted.
After host storage/mount
preparation, the wrapper submits a digest-pinned private plan through the
supported `identity_sled.provision_container` operation. The owner atomically
creates fresh current-schema state and binds it to the new native instance;
legacy persistence and record fields are not imported. Existing external
capability policy remains in force. Normal provisioning starts through
`touch_session`; `--no-start` leaves the fresh identity parked. Only verified
completion receives a boot-ready marker.

If creation fails, `op-identity-root seed-inspect NAME` reports sanitized
receipt metadata and recovery guidance without mounting, formatting or
retrying device-add. Preserve the receipt, base, leaf and mappings until the
recorded intent and actual membership have been reconciled.

Preparing or changing the live seed is a separate operator action. The helper
does not set or clear SEEDING, format the partition, or unmount an unrelated
source mount. Once leaves depend on a seed, that seed must remain unchanged.
At boot, the host storage service uses `seed-readonly` to verify the physical
partition identity and existing SEEDING state, then restore its volatile block
read-only flag before restoring opted-in roots. This never changes filesystem
membership or the SEEDING flag.
The current source change has not been deployed or validated with concurrent
live containers on the fresh base. The September 30 file-backed and physical
seed experiments did demonstrate independent writes, peer-active remounts and
cold loop recreation using distinct read-only views of the same seed on this
kernel. That evidence does not validate this new image/layout or a full host
reboot. There is no fallback to copied seeds if a kernel rejects the shared
arrangement. The owner's current sequencing instruction defers all tests until
after deployment; a successful build alone is not a workflow validation.

See the [Btrfs seeding documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

name: verification-before-completion
description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
---

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

[Skill file: /srv/git/odbus-verified/.claude/skills/agent-self-evaluation/SKILL.md]
---
name: agent-self-evaluation
description: Use after completing any non-trivial task. The agent self-rates its output on 5 axes — accuracy, completeness, clarity, actionability, conciseness — with concrete evidence per criterion. Produces a structured 1-5 scorecard with specific improvement suggestions.
origin: ECC
---

# Agent Self-Evaluation

After completing a complex task, the agent pauses to rate its own output against a structured 5-axis rubric. This is NOT a pass/fail gate — it's a deliberate reflection step that catches omissions, flags overconfidence, and surface areas for improvement before the user has to.

## When to Activate

- After writing code that spans 3+ files or 50+ lines
- After completing a multi-step workflow (implement → test → review)
- After a debugging session that involved 3+ attempts
- After producing a design document, architecture decision, or written analysis
- When the user asks "how good was that?" or "rate yourself"
- At the end of any session Stop hook (if configured — see `references/hook-integration.md`)

## Core Concepts

### The 5 Evaluation Axes

| Axis | Question | What it catches |
|---|---|---|
| **Accuracy** | Are the facts, claims, and outputs correct? | Hallucinations, wrong API names, incorrect syntax, false statements |
| **Completeness** | Did it cover everything the user asked for? | Missed edge cases, unhandled error paths, forgotten requirements, skipped subtasks |
| **Clarity** | Is the explanation understandable and well-structured? | Confusing explanations, jargon without definition, missing context, rambling |
| **Actionability** | Can the user act on the output immediately? | Vague suggestions, missing steps, "you should X" without showing how, no verification path |
| **Conciseness** | Did it use the minimum words/tokens needed? | Redundancy, over-explanation, repeating the user's question verbatim, filler content |

### Scoring Scale

```
5 — Exceptional: no reasonable improvement possible
4 — Good: minor nits only, no substantive gaps
3 — Adequate: meets the request but has a notable weakness on at least one axis
2 — Weak: has a clear gap that affects usability or correctness
1 — Poor: fundamentally misses the request or contains significant errors
```

### The Evidence Rule

Every score below 5 MUST cite specific evidence. A score of 3 cannot just say "could be better" — it must say exactly what is missing or wrong. The mantra: **"Show the gap, don't just name it."**

## Workflow

### Step 1: Collect the Raw Material

Gather what you'll evaluate:

```
- The original user request (read back from conversation)
- Your final response/output (the deliverable)
- Any tool outputs that verify correctness (test results, exit codes, lint output)
- Any user feedback received during the task (corrections, "try again", "that's not right")
```

### Step 2: Score Each Axis Independently

Work through the 5 axes one at a time. For each:

1. Read the axis question
2. Find evidence (or lack of evidence) in the output
3. Assign a score 1-5
4. If score < 5, write a one-sentence improvement note citing the gap

Do NOT average the scores in your head first and then work backwards. Score each axis fresh.

### Step 3: Produce the Evaluation Report

Use the template from `templates/evaluation-report.md`. The report must include:

```
- One-line summary
- 5-axis scorecard (score + evidence per axis)
- Overall score (simple average, rounded to 1 decimal)
- 1-3 specific improvements ranked by impact
- Self-check: "Would the user agree with this assessment?"
```

### Step 4: Apply the Improvement

If any axis scored 3 or below:

1. State what you would do differently
2. If the gap is fixable in < 30 seconds (missing link, unclear phrasing), fix it now
3. If the gap requires rework, flag it explicitly: "This axis scored [reason] because [evidence]. Re-running with [specific fix] would likely raise it to [score]."

## Code Examples

### Example: Good Evaluation (Score 4+)

```
Task: Add retry logic to HTTP client

Scorecard:
  Accuracy:    5 — All API calls correct. Verified: retries use
                  exponential backoff. No hallucinated methods.
  Completeness: 4 — Covered happy path + 3 error cases. Missing:
                  timeout handling for hung connections.
  Clarity:      5 — Code comments explain backoff formula.
                  PR description links to incident that motivated this.
  Actionability:5 — Single merge. No follow-up tasks. Tests pass.
  Conciseness:  4 — 47 lines total. The retry loop could be extracted
                  into a helper to drop ~8 lines.

Overall: 4.6 — One gap (timeout handling). Fix before merging.
```

### Example: Weak Evaluation (Score 2-3)

```
Task: Add retry logic to HTTP client

Scorecard:
  Accuracy:    2 — Used urllib3 which doesn't match our
                  httpx-based codebase. Wrong library.
  Completeness: 3 — Works for GET. POST/PUT not handled (user
                  said "all HTTP requests").
  Clarity:      4 — Code is readable. Good variable names.
  Actionability:2 — "Add tests" mentioned but no test file created.
                  User has to write tests before merging.
  Conciseness:  3 — 120 lines. The retry config is duplicated in
                  3 places instead of one shared RetryConfig object.

Overall: 2.8 — Wrong library used. Needs httpx rewrite.
  Fix accuracy first (switch to httpx), then extend to all
  HTTP methods, then consolidate config.
```

## Anti-Patterns

### "Everything is a 5"

```
FAIL: Accuracy:    5 — All good.
   Completeness: 5 — Everything covered.
   Clarity:      5 — Clear.
```

No evidence cited. This is self-congratulation, not evaluation. A real 5 requires proving there's nothing to improve.

### Over-penalizing for scope creep

```
FAIL: Completeness: 2 — Didn't handle WebSocket connections or
   gRPC streaming (user didn't ask for these)
```

Only evaluate against what the user actually requested, not what you could have additionally built.

### Using the evaluation to re-litigate

```
FAIL: "As I said earlier, this approach is wrong. Score: 1"
```

The evaluation is about the delivered output, not about re-arguing design decisions that were already made. If the approach was wrong, that should have been caught before delivery.

### Mixing personal preference with objective gaps

```
FAIL: "Score: 3. I don't like Python decorators."
```

"Don't like" is not evidence. Cite a concrete readability, testability, or correctness concern, or leave the score at 4+.

## Best Practices

- **Evaluate the output, not the process.** The user cares about what you delivered, not how many iterations you took.
- **One improvement per weak axis.** Don't list 5 things for one axis — pick the highest-impact gap.
- **Tie improvements to user impact.** "Missing error handling means the user's API call will crash silently" beats "add error handling."
- **Be specific about what 'fixed' looks like.** "Re-run with httpx transport configured for retries" beats "fix the library issue."
- **Use tool outputs as evidence.** If tests passed, cite them. If lint is clean, cite it. Don't guess — grep for the proof.
- **If you can't find any gaps, try harder.** A perfect score across all 5 axes is rare. Ask: "If I were the user, what would annoy me about this output?"

## Related Skills

- `agent-eval` — Head-to-head comparison of different coding agents on benchmark tasks
- `verification-loop` — Systematic verification of outputs against expected results
- `security-review` — Security-focused code review checklist

[deploy/runit/incus-ct-chatbot/run#C983]
1:#!/bin/sh
2:# The transitional control-plane chatbot: the bridge needs a live identity
3:# session, so this container starts at boot until identities replace it.
4:# runit longrun for Incus container: the control-plane chatbot (b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28)
5:exec 2>&1
6:
7:wait_dep() {
8:    dep="$1"
9:    sv start "$dep" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
10:    i=0
11:    until sv check "$dep" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
12:        i=$((i + 1))
13:        if [ "$i" -ge 90 ]; then
14:            echo "dependency $dep not ready after 90s" >&2
15:            exit 1
16:        fi
17:        sleep 1
18:    done
19:}
20:
21:wait_dep incusd
22:# Once the chatbot runs on its own identity root, identity-roots mounts that
23:# root and its lungs; starting the instance first would boot it on an empty
24:# rootfs directory. identity-roots becomes ready even with no identity devices.
25:wait_dep identity-roots
26:
27:NAME='b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28'
28:# Switch only after the host storage owner has verified a completed named
29:# replacement. An incomplete candidate does not retire the existing identity.
30:if [ -f /var/lib/opdbus-runtime/seed-identities/3tchedChatbot/boot-ready.json ]; then
31:    NAME=3tchedChatbot
32:fi
33:
34:i=0
35:until incus info >/dev/null 2>&1; do
36:    i=$((i + 1))
37:    if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then
38:        echo "incusd API not ready" >&2
39:        exit 1
40:    fi
41:    sleep 1
42:done
43:
44:# runit owns lifecycle
45:incus config set "$NAME" boot.autostart=false 2>/dev/null || true
46:
47:if ! incus list -f csv -c ns 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NAME},RUNNING$"; then
48:    # Only opted-in, explicitly paired storage uses the upgrade lifecycle.
49:    # Keep this before start; never replace a running container's OS view.
50:    pair=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/.provisioning/$NAME.upgrade.json
51:    if [ -e "$pair" ] || [ -L "$pair" ]; then
52:        /usr/local/libexec/3tched/sync-instance-upgrade boot "$NAME" || exit 1
53:        expected=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$NAME/rootfs
54:        incus --force-local query "/1.0/instances/$NAME" | jq -e \
55:            '.devices.root.type=="disk" and .devices.root.path=="/" and .devices.root.pool=="identity-roots"' >/dev/null &&
56:            [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$expected" -o FSTYPE)" = overlay ] &&
57:            findmnt -rn -M "$expected" -o OPTIONS | grep -Eq '(^|,)ro(,|$)' || {
58:            echo "paired container needs its read-only overlay mounted at $expected; provisioning incomplete" >&2
59:            exit 1
60:        }
61:    fi
62:    echo "starting container $NAME"
63:    if ! incus start "$NAME"; then
64:        echo "incus start failed for $NAME" >&2
65:        incus info "$NAME" --show-log 2>&1 | tail -n 40 || true
66:        exit 1
67:    fi
68:fi
69:
70:i=0
71:until incus list -f csv -c ns 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NAME},RUNNING$"; do
72:    i=$((i + 1))
73:    if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then
74:        echo "container $NAME failed to reach RUNNING" >&2
75:        incus info "$NAME" --show-log 2>&1 | tail -n 40 || true
76:        exit 1
77:    fi
78:    sleep 1
79:done
80:echo "container $NAME is RUNNING"
81:/usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal incus-ct-chatbot
82:
83:# one-shot console log snapshot into the runit log (non-blocking)
84:incus console "$NAME" --show-log 2>/dev/null | tail -n 80 || true
85:
86:cleanup() {
87:    echo "stopping container $NAME (runit down)"
88:    incus stop "$NAME" --timeout 30 2>/dev/null || incus stop "$NAME" --force 2>/dev/null || true
89:}
90:trap cleanup TERM INT HUP
91:
92:# stay up while CT is RUNNING; exit 1 so runit restarts if CT dies under us
93:while incus list -f csv -c ns 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NAME},RUNNING$"; do
94:    sleep 5
95:done
96:echo "container $NAME left RUNNING — exiting for restart"
97:exit 1

#!/bin/sh
# The transitional control-plane chatbot: the bridge needs a live identity
# session, so this container starts at boot until identities replace it.
# runit longrun for Incus container: the control-plane chatbot (b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28)
exec 2>&1

wait_dep() {
    dep="$1"
    sv start "$dep" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    i=0
    until sv check "$dep" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        i=$((i + 1))
        if [ "$i" -ge 90 ]; then
            echo "dependency $dep not ready after 90s" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        sleep 1
    done
}

wait_dep incusd
# Once the chatbot runs on its own identity root, identity-roots mounts that
# root and its lungs; starting the instance first would boot it on an empty
# rootfs directory. identity-roots becomes ready even with no identity devices.
wait_dep identity-roots

NAME='b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28'
# Switch only after the host storage owner has verified a completed named
# replacement. An incomplete candidate does not retire the existing identity.
if [ -f /var/lib/opdbus-runtime/seed-identities/3tchedChatbot/boot-ready.json ]; then
    NAME=3tchedChatbot
fi

i=0
until incus info >/dev/null 2>&1; do
    i=$((i + 1))
    if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then
        echo "incusd API not ready" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done

# runit owns lifecycle
incus config set "$NAME" boot.autostart=false 2>/dev/null || true

if ! incus list -f csv -c ns 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NAME},RUNNING$"; then
    # Only opted-in, explicitly paired storage uses the upgrade lifecycle.
    # Keep this before start; never replace a running container's OS view.
    pair=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/.provisioning/$NAME.upgrade.json
    if [ -e "$pair" ] || [ -L "$pair" ]; then
        /usr/local/libexec/3tched/sync-instance-upgrade boot "$NAME" || exit 1
        expected=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$NAME/rootfs
        incus --force-local query "/1.0/instances/$NAME" | jq -e \
            '.devices.root.type=="disk" and .devices.root.path=="/" and .devices.root.pool=="identity-roots"' >/dev/null &&
            [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$expected" -o FSTYPE)" = overlay ] &&
            findmnt -rn -M "$expected" -o OPTIONS | grep -Eq '(^|,)ro(,|$)' || {
            echo "paired container needs its read-only overlay mounted at $expected; provisioning incomplete" >&2
            exit 1
        }
    fi
    echo "starting container $NAME"
    if ! incus start "$NAME"; then
        echo "incus start failed for $NAME" >&2
        incus info "$NAME" --show-log 2>&1 | tail -n 40 || true
        exit 1
    fi
fi

i=0
until incus list -f csv -c ns 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NAME},RUNNING$"; do
    i=$((i + 1))
    if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then
        echo "container $NAME failed to reach RUNNING" >&2
        incus info "$NAME" --show-log 2>&1 | tail -n 40 || true
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done
echo "container $NAME is RUNNING"
/usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal incus-ct-chatbot

# one-shot console log snapshot into the runit log (non-blocking)
incus console "$NAME" --show-log 2>/dev/null | tail -n 80 || true

cleanup() {
    echo "stopping container $NAME (runit down)"
    incus stop "$NAME" --timeout 30 2>/dev/null || incus stop "$NAME" --force 2>/dev/null || true
}
trap cleanup TERM INT HUP

# stay up while CT is RUNNING; exit 1 so runit restarts if CT dies under us
while incus list -f csv -c ns 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NAME},RUNNING$"; do
    sleep 5
done
echo "container $NAME left RUNNING — exiting for restart"
exit 1

#!/bin/sh
# Host storage owner: remount/receive existing GPT members, never mint/start.
set -eu
fail() { printf 'restore-chatbot-root: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
check_only=false
if [ "${1:-}" = --check ]; then check_only=true; shift; fi
[ "$#" -le 1 ] || fail 'usage: restore-chatbot-root [--check] [NAME]'
name=${1:-3tchedChatbot}
printf '%s' "$name" | grep -Eq '^(3tchedCtlChatbot|3tchedChatbot|ID-[1-9][0-9]*)$' && [ "${#name}" -le 63 ] || fail 'invalid chatbot selector'
# The name selects the native target; the same existing UUID/session/key and
# storage receipts below are required for both the legacy alias and ID-N.
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host root required'
sid=b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28
key=[REDACTED:opaque-base64]
pool=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/3tched-pool
receipt=$pool/.provisioning/$name.boot.json
binding=$pool/.provisioning/$name.incus.json
disk=$pool/.provisioning/$name.json
root=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$name/rootfs
view=$pool/.mounts/$name/root-view
seed_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/seed-layer
upgrade_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade-layer
readback() { timeout --kill-after=5s 30s "$@"; }
secure_path() (
    path=$1
    [ "$(realpath -e -- "$path")" = "$path" ] || fail "noncanonical path: $path"
    while :; do
        [ ! -L "$path" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u -- "$path")" = 0 ] &&
            [ $((0$(stat -c %a -- "$path") & 022)) -eq 0 ] || fail "unsafe owner/mode: $path"
        [ "$path" != / ] || break
        path=$(dirname -- "$path")
    done
)
secure_path "$pool"
[ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$pool")" = 0:0 ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o UUID)" = a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M / -o UUID)" != a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd ] ||
    fail 'canonical loop pool is not mounted on its pinned filesystem'
secure_path "$pool/.provisioning"
[ -d "$pool/.provisioning" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$pool/.provisioning")" = 0:0:700 ] ||
    fail 'preparation receipt directory must be private'
for file in "$receipt" "$binding" "$disk"; do
    secure_path "$file"
    [ -f "$file" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$file")" = 0:0:600 ] || fail "unsafe preparation receipt: $file"
done
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" '
    .version==1 and .name==$name and .session_id==$sid and
    .identity_registered==true and .restore_existing_pair==true
' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'chatbot boot attestation differs'
# The boot opt-in is not identity authority. Match the host preparation's
# existing native UUID/session/key and storage paths before any mount action.
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" --arg key "$key" --arg root "$root" --arg view "$view" '
    .version==1 and .name==$name and .session_id==$sid and .phase=="root-bound" and
    .root_bound==true and .root_view_readonly==true and .upgrade_paired==true and
    .threetched_root==$root and .root_view==$view and .instance.name==$name and .instance.type=="container" and
    .instance.config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and .instance.config["user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key"]==$key and
    (.instance.config["volatile.uuid"]|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$"))
' "$binding" >/dev/null || fail 'chatbot preparation pins differ'
uuid=$(jq -er '.instance.config["volatile.uuid"]' "$binding")
jq -e --arg uuid "$uuid" '
    (has("instance_uuid")|not) or .instance_uuid==$uuid
' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'boot native UUID differs'
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg image "$pool/$name.img" --arg root "$pool/.mounts/$name/root" \
    --arg upgrade "$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade" '
    .name==$name and .layout=="raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1" and .phase=="filesystems-prepared" and
    .filesystem_prepared==true and .image==$image and .root_mount==$root and .upgrade_mount==$upgrade
' "$disk" >/dev/null || fail 'disk preparation pins differ'
image=$pool/$name.img
secure_path "$image"
[ -f "$image" ] && [ "$(stat -c %i "$image")" = "$(jq -r .image_inode "$disk")" ] &&
    [ "$(stat -c %s "$image")" = "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$disk")" ] || fail 'image pins differ'
instance=$(readback incus --force-local query "/1.0/instances/$name?project=default") || fail 'native instance readback failed'
printf '%s\n' "$instance" | jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" --arg key "$key" --arg uuid "$uuid" '
    .name==$name and .type=="container" and .config["volatile.uuid"]==$uuid and
    .config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and .config["user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key"]==$key and
    .config["security.privileged"]=="false" and .config["security.protection.shift"]=="true" and
    .config["boot.autostart"]=="false" and .profiles==["3tched-lungs"] and
    .devices.root.type=="disk" and .devices.root.path=="/" and .devices.root.pool=="identity-roots" and
    ((.status=="Stopped" and .status_code==102) or (.status=="Running" and .status_code==103))
' >/dev/null || fail 'native chatbot UUID/session/key/policy differs'
state=$(printf '%s\n' "$instance" | jq -er .status)
# Select the activated closure deliberately. When invoked from a source or
# received release, use that helper's sibling; never fall through to base copies.
self=$(realpath -e -- "$0") || fail 'cannot resolve restore helper'
helper_dir=$(dirname -- "$self")
case "$helper_dir" in
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched)
        helper_dir=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers ;;
esac
sync_helper=$helper_dir/sync-instance-upgrade
case "$self" in
    */deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/restore-chatbot-root)
        sync_helper=$helper_dir/../../scripts/sync-instance-upgrade.sh ;;
esac
sync_helper=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_SYNC_INSTANCE_UPGRADE_HELPER:-$sync_helper}") || fail 'selected sync helper absent'
secure_path "$sync_helper"
[ -f "$sync_helper" ] && [ -x "$sync_helper" ] || fail 'selected sync helper not executable'
if [ "$state" = Running ]; then
    # A service restart observes only; it must not replace a running guest's lowers.
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FSTYPE)" = overlay ] || fail 'running root is not overlay'
    options=$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FS-OPTIONS) || fail 'cannot inspect running root'
    case ",$options," in *,"lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer",*) ;; *) fail 'running root lower pins differ' ;; esac
    case ",$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o VFS-OPTIONS)," in *,ro,*) ;; *) fail 'running root is not read-only' ;; esac
    exit 0
fi
[ "$check_only" != true ] || exit 0
exec "$sync_helper" boot "$name"
